question: Should OpenClaw adopt `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate` and the shared query-template helper as a permanent opt-in config and plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The implementation adds user-facing config and public provider/SDK surface; repository policy requires owner judgment because those compatibility and ownership choices cannot be inferred from tests or model documentation.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Opt-In Contract
options.body: Keep the setting default-false, centralize templates once, and expose only the minimum API needed by supported embedding providers.

options.title: Keep The Policy Provider-Local
options.body: Avoid a shared public helper and implement the opt-in behavior only inside the bundled and generic OpenAI-compatible provider owners.

options.title: Decline The New Surface
options.body: Retain raw OpenAI-compatible queries and leave instruction formatting to provider servers or external proxies.

recommendation.title: Approve A Narrow Opt-In Contract
recommendation.body: Keep the setting default-false, centralize templates once, and expose only the minimum API needed by supported embedding providers.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows the strongest ownership of the memory embedding adapter and provider boundaries affected by this API decision.
